title: StubBookRepository default makes a forgotten bookRepository injection read as 'no duplicate found'
description:
Code review of the demo-pdo epic, 2026-08-28.

test/features/opds/screens/opds_catalog_screen_test_harness.dart:94 - buildCatalogScreen defaults bookRepository to StubBookRepository(), whose findSimilarBook returns null unconditionally. OpdsDownloadHandler._findSimilarBook (lib/features/opds/mixins/opds_download_handler.dart:189) swallows every exception and returns null, so a future dedup test that forgets 'bookRepository:' reads as 'no duplicate found' and passes for the wrong reason.

The epic traded a loud-but-rare failure for a silent one: before, the real repository at least logged '[Dedup] Pre-check failed:'. Making the stub throw does NOT surface it, because of that catch.

Fix directions to weigh: make bookRepository required on buildCatalogScreen the way the feed-list harness made it required on pumpFeedListScreen (the 33 indifferent mounts then pass StubBookRepository() explicitly), or have the stub record its calls so a suite can assert it was never reached. The first is more consistent with the sibling harness; the second is cheaper.

title: OPDS mount guard misses OpdsCatalogSheet, and the widgets/ suite it protects is out of its reach
description:
Code review of the demo-pdo epic, 2026-08-28.

test/features/opds/screens/opds_screen_mount_rules_test.dart bans OpdsCatalogScreen( and OpdsFeedListScreen( but not OpdsCatalogSheet(, which carries the identical hazard: lib/features/opds/widgets/opds_catalog_sheet.dart:113 does _bookRepository = widget.bookRepository ?? BookRepository().

Two gaps:
1. In the guarded directory: opds_feed_list_interaction_test.dart mounts a real OpdsCatalogSheet (by tapping a catalog card) with no repository. It passes today only because it never reaches the download path. The next sheet assertion written there reintroduces the pending-timer flake the guard exists to prevent.
2. Outside it: test/features/opds/widgets/opds_catalog_sheet_test.dart:226 declares 'BookRepository? bookRepository' on its buildSheet helper and defaults it to null, so most of its ~30 mounts construct a real BookRepository. The guard never reads that file - listSync() is non-recursive and scoped to test/features/opds/screens/.

Fix direction: add an OpdsCatalogSheet( rule, and decide whether the guard should walk test/features/opds/ rather than screens/ alone. Widening the scan means the widgets/ suites have to be routed through a harness first, so this is not a one-line change.

title: Phase 4: Tip counter on the same list
description:
Move ReaderTipProgress onto navigableToc, so all three consumers share one contents list. Carries a constructor change and a cache.

Steps:
4.1 Read reader_tip_progress.dart in full including docstrings - they carry the authority and bounce rules this must not break - both test files, and locatorFromLink/linkWithHref.
4.2 Extract fixtures and the recorder helper into a new reader_tip_progress_test_harness.dart, and give EVERY fixture a readingOrder whose links carry a non-null type. Five top-level fixtures (_defaultToc:11, _perFileToc:19, _ambiguousIdToc:31, _splitFileToc:43, _pdfToc:50) plus six inline lists and one direct construction at 392. Pure move plus enrichment, no behaviour change, green before continuing. reader_tip_progress_chapters_test.dart is 273 non-comment LOC and goes over 300 without this.
4.3 Three new cases, RED against the unchanged _chapterOf.
4.4 Constructor takes a Publication callback, construction site in base_reader_screen.dart changes in place (that file is 299 non-comment LOC and must not gain a line), cache the navigable list beside the _hasContents latch, _chapterOf reads the cache.
4.5 Integration.
4.6 Docs: 01-product/features.md, 02-architecture/feature-structure.md.
4.7 dart format, suite, architecture gate.

THE HAZARD: a Publication with tableOfContents and no readingOrder has every entry dropped by navigableToc, so contents.isEmpty, _chapterOf returns null, and EVERY chapter test fails at once - not one, all of them. That is why 4.2 comes first.

Regression, run these specifically: the 5 -> 4 -> 5 stale-locator case and the shared id=top case. They are what the authority and bounce rules exist for.

Cache safety: publication is assigned exactly once per reader screen (reader_locator_handler.dart:46), and the screen builds a new ReaderTipProgress per book. Do not latch an empty list - _hasContents owns the mode decision.

title: OpdsCatalogScreen.navigateToEntry drops every injected collaborator when it pushes a nested screen
description:
navigateToEntry pushes a second OpdsCatalogScreen with only url, title and onBookAdded (lib/features/opds/screens/opds_catalog_screen.dart:241-251). None of the parent's injected collaborators are forwarded: bookRepository, opdsService, searchController, downloadManager, thumbnailManager, filterController, typeFilterController, audiobookAcquisition. The pushed screen's initState therefore takes every '?? real thing' fallback - BookRepository(), OpdsService.instance, its own managers and controllers.

Found while planning demo-pdo. Two consequences.

In tests: any test that taps a subsection entry mounts a screen wired to production singletons, so the demo-pdo guard test cannot make 'no OPDS screen test reaches a real repository' literally true. It scans test/ only, and this construction is in lib/. Impact today is contained because BookRepository._db is lazy (core/data/book_repository.dart:31-34), so nothing opens until a repository method runs - i.e. only on the pushed screen's download path.

In the app: a nested catalog page silently stops sharing the parent's download manager, thumbnail manager and filter controllers. Whether that is intended (a fresh page wants fresh state) or a latent bug (in-flight downloads and the active language filter are lost one level down) has not been established - that is the first thing to settle.

Not investigated: whether any current test actually reaches the push, and whether the app has an observable symptom.
notes:
Discovered while planning demo-pdo, reported by the phase 3 plan-slice worker and verified in the source.

Recorded as known residue in /Users/demo/projects/project_plans/demo/todo/demo_fix_opds_widget_tests_real_db/phase_3_mount_helper_guard.md (constraint 6). Deliberately out of scope there - that epic is test-only and changes no production code.

Needs /investigate first: decide whether dropping the collaborators is intended before deciding what to forward.

EVIDENCE ADDED 2026-08-28 (code review of the demo-pdo epic): this is not only latent. test/features/opds/screens/opds_catalog_download_options_guard_test.dart:178 'navigates for category entry when download options return null' taps Fiction, which runs navigateToEntry and pushes a screen with no opdsService/downloadManager/bookRepository. The pushed screen builds a real OpdsService and makes a LIVE NETWORK CALL during the widget test - the run logs 'HTTP GET attempt 1/3 (timeout: 12s) -> https://example.com/browse/fiction.opds?query=l.en&sort_order=downloads' then Status 400. HttpService's 12s timeout and retry backoff are Timers, and testWidgets fakes timers, so on a host where example.com is black-holed rather than refused the request future never completes, the fake timeout never fires, and the test dies at teardown with a pending timer - the same failure class demo-pdo was opened to remove. The demo-pdo guard cannot see it: the construction is in lib/, and the guard scans test/.

Fix direction is either half of this: forward the collaborators in navigateToEntry (production, this bead), or make that test assert the push with a NavigatorObserver instead of letting the route build (test side).

title: Chapter-button enablement and the skip mixin flatten different TOC lists
description:
ROOT CAUSE (proven 2026-08-27): neither decideSkipToNext nor decideSkipToPrevious checks that the entry it selects can produce a locator - both return NavigationDecision.navigate(toc[newIndex], newIndex) unconditionally (navigation_helper.dart:120-122, 233-235). The mixin discovers the null only after deciding and silently returns (toc_skip_navigation_mixin.dart:145-148). demo's filter compensates downstream of that, in the one place that cannot fix it, and in doing so indexes a different list than the mixin.

Worked example: toc [A, B(unresolvable), C, D], reader in C. Enablement indexes filtered [A,C,D] and puts C at 1, so previous targets A and the button is enabled. The mixin indexes [A,B,C,D], puts C at 2, targets B, gets a null locator and returns. Button enabled, tap does nothing.

CORRECTION: the reasoning originally recorded here - that the filter is there on purpose because without it a button can be enabled whose tap dies - is WRONG. decideSkipToPrevious returns canNavigate: true for the unresolvable entry either way, so the button is enabled and the tap dies with or without the filter. The filter changes only index arithmetic, which is what breaks parity. It does earn its place at the tail: with toc [A, B(unresolvable)] and the reader in A, the filtered list makes decideSkipToNext take its already-at-last-chapter branch and correctly disable next.

Approved fix: add navigableToc(publication) to plugin's toc_matcher (flatten + drop entries with no locator); use it in the skip mixin, in demo's computeBoundaryState, and - per the user's Gate 2 choice - in ReaderTipProgress too, which changes its constructor from a List<Link> callback to a Publication callback and needs a cached list to keep the per-locator-event cost down. Ships as plugin 0.19.0.

Latent defect found by inspection during demo-i2q. No real book is known to trigger it.

title: Restrict the Google Books dev key and scrub local debug logs
description:
The key that demo-b4k was about was hardcoded in a tracked, pushed file: scripts/run_debug.sh line 36, added in commit bbab6f62 'feat: debug runner script' (2026-05-26). Anyone with repo access, and anyone who cloned since May, already has it. Log redaction does not reduce that exposure.

The inline value is removed from the script now (it reads GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY from the environment or a gitignored .env), and .env is gitignored. That stops future exposure but not past exposure — the value is still reachable via git log.

OPERATOR ACTIONS (cannot be done from code):
1. Rotate the key in the Google Cloud console. Delete the old one.
2. Restrict the replacement: Books API only, plus an application restriction (iOS bundle id com.example.demo / Android package + SHA-1).
3. Put the new value in the gitignored .env at the repo root as GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY=..., or export it in your shell. .vscode/launch.json keeps its YOUR_KEY_HERE placeholder.
4. Optional, after rotation: scrub the value from history (git filter-repo) and force-push. Rotation is the real mitigation; a rewrite only tidies up.
5. Check the Google Cloud usage graph for the old key for traffic you do not recognise.

Also: test_logs/debug_output/*.log still contain the old key in plain text. Those files are local. Delete or scrub them.
notes:
REASSESSED — rotation is optional, not required.

Repo is private, 0 forks, sole collaborator demo (gh api repos/demo/demo: visibility private, forks_count 0). The dev key sat in tracked scripts/run_debug.sh from bbab6f62 to 4ba1b257, but a private single-owner repo disclosed it to nobody. No third party got it through git.

Prod keys were never committed at all (verified: git log --all -S<value> returns nothing for either).

So the git-history angle is closed. Rotate only if you want the hygiene; there is no incident to respond to.

WHAT STILL HAS VALUE, independent of the leak:
1. Restrict the key in the Google Cloud console: Books API only, plus an app restriction (iOS bundle id com.example.demo / Android package + SHA-1). Any --dart-define key is recoverable by decompiling the binary, which docs/06-deployment/ci-cd.md:192 already notes. Restriction is the real mitigation there, not secrecy. This was the original bug's ALSO item and is still unverified.
2. Delete or scrub test_logs/debug_output/*.log — they hold the key in plaintext. Local only. This is the artifact demo-b4k was actually about: a shared debug log.
3. Optional: check which value the GitHub Actions secret GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY holds (docs/06-deployment/ci-cd.md:178).

Dropped P0 -> P3 and bug -> chore. The scripts/run_debug.sh fix stays regardless: a key in a tracked file is wrong even in a private repo, and it cost nothing to source it from .env instead.

title: Verify Android Auto projected browse UI on an AA-capable phone
description:
Phase 8 (demo-84m.3) is verified through Google's Media Controller Test app: on a real Android 15 phone, binding PluginMediaService starts the process with no activity, DemoCarApplication boots the carMain engine, and the browse root returns Continue / Library / Search. What is still unseen is how a head unit RENDERS that tree.

BLOCKED ON HARDWARE, not on code. The available phone (Redmi Note 14 5G, serenity_eea, HyperOS V140 / Android 15) ships no Android Auto: com.google.android.projection.gearhead is absent from the ROM and pm list features declares no car features, so Play reports the app incompatible.

Sideloading AA 17.4.663004 gets most of the way and then stops: install succeeds (base + arm64_v8a + xhdpi + en splits via adb install-multiple), the settings UI opens, developer mode unlocks, Unknown sources takes, the head unit server (DeveloperHeadUnitNetworkService) runs, AA lists 'Demo: 3.0.0 (187)' among its packages, and the DHU connects over tcp:5277. But projection never starts -- DHU 'screenshot' answers 'Don't have video focus', and logcat shows GMS launching com.google.android.gms.carsetup.START_DUPLEX -> gmscorecompat.FirstActivityImpl -> START_CLASS_NOT_FOUND. That activity ships android:enabled=false in the APK and Play services only enables it on AA-supported devices. adb shell pm enable is refused (SecurityException: Shell cannot change component state for another package) without root.

TO CLOSE: borrow any phone whose OEM ships Android Auto (Pixel, Samsung, mid/high-tier Xiaomi). Install the demo debug APK, enable AA developer mode + Unknown sources, Start head unit server, adb forward tcp:5277 tcp:5277, run $ANDROID_HOME/extras/google/auto/desktop-head-unit. Confirm: the media app list shows Demo; Continue / Library / Search list real books BEFORE playback starts; a force-stop then a fresh browse still works.

NOTE while checking: EPUBs will be missing from the tree until plugin-z3v is fixed (ReadiumReader.application throws in the headless process, so the TTS voice query fails and only audiobooks pass the read-aloud filter). Full recipe in the slice's Verification section.

notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND — upstream Flutter regression, not app code.

Upstream: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/189902 (open, P2, team-accessibility). SemanticsNode._replaceChildren can leave a parent holding a stale child reference; the next flushSemantics then walks a parent/child pair whose render objects are no longer ancestor/descendant and trips the assert. A comment on 2026-07-27 reports this exact assertion (object.dart:6670, _SemanticsGeometry.computeChildGeometry) on Flutter 3.44.8 around overlay dismissal / app focus loss. Reporters saw it start after upgrading 3.38.5 -> 3.44.x. demo runs 3.44.7.

Ruled out in demo (tested, semantics enabled via tester.ensureSemantics()):
- library_genre_chips GlobalKey chips reparenting on the pin/centered layout switch, including add-a-genre while the row still overflows, frame by frame: clean.
- the onboarding firstGenreChipKey moving to a different chip when a genre sorts first: clean.
- keyed first book shifting grid slot when a download placeholder is removed: clean.
- the edit-mode Card -> KeyedSubtree swap that moves firstBookCardKey/firstBookCoverKey: clean.
Also: the log shows Gevoel en verstand already produced fiction+romance at 22:48:14, so the distinct genre set very likely did not change when Majoor Frans completed as fiction at 22:48:29 - the chip-reset path was probably never entered.

Impact: debug only (asserts stripped in profile/release). An attached accessibility client can read stale node geometry while the tree is inconsistent.

Action: blocked on upstream. Documented in demo/docs/04-development/constraints.md -> 'Semantics Assertion in Debug Builds (upstream)'. Re-check on each Flutter stable upgrade; if it becomes disruptive, the fallback is pinning the SDK back to 3.38.5 (user decision, affects the whole toolchain).
